capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Relays Volvo US: AWD versions keep the 78 kWh battery; the 78 kWh pack is the XC40/C40 Recharge Twin pack since launch (2021-2024).

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: EV Database (European MY22 car, same 78 kWh pack): 75.0 kWh usable. Wikipedia also gives 78 gross / 75 usable for the C40.

chemistry.notes: EV Database: NMC cathode, pouch, 108s3p (same cell family on all 78 kWh packs).

nominal_voltage_class.notes: EV Database: 400 V nominal and architecture.

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: Volvo support says the battery is preconditioned when a rapid charger is set as the Google Maps destination (read via search excerpt; page 403), and EV Database says preconditioning can start automatically via navigation. No manual control found in any Volvo page read, but no North American owner manual could be opened (volvocars.com returns 403), so a manual control cannot be ruled out.

dc_max_kw.notes: Estimated: Same 78 kWh pack and 150 kW peak as the 2024 Twin that Volvo US states at 150 kW; Wikipedia gives 150 kW for the 2021-2023 pack.

ac_max_kw.notes: Estimated: NRCan and EPA both rate the 2025-2026 EX40 at 8 h on 240 V (NRCan row EX40 / EX40 Twin, recharge time 8 h), which fits an 11 kW onboard charger for a 79-82 kWh pack. Volvo Canada support (EX40 charging time, read only as a search excerpt, page 403) says the highest AC output is 11 kW, and EV Database lists 11 kW (European 3-phase). Older model years carried over (same CMA charger); no North American page opened states it directly.
